requirement: - **Army sets are traded at once, at every level.** A set of Anchors (5), Compasses (8) or Lanterns (15) never grows, so holding it gains nothing and risks the Squall and the hand limit. A seat whose hand makes an army set therefore trades a set that turn. Which one, when the hand makes several (they may share Wilds, and only one is traded a turn): the army set adding most armies, unless a Surge or Raid set is worth more now and its own rule below says to trade it; a Surge set is worth this turn's income, a Raid set its expected saving in attacking armies.

requirement: - **The Surge set waits for a big turn** *(A7)*. Three Surges add the turn's income once more (country part and island bonuses): worth exactly the income `I`, so more as the seat grows. From Normal up the computer trades a Surge set when any of these holds, and otherwise keeps it: - its income is at least `SURGE_INCOME` (8); - its hand holds 4 or more cards, so the next capture would risk a discard or more; - the Squall is in the draw pile and the pile holds `SQUALL_PILE` (15) cards or fewer, so each own draw has a 1 in 15 or greater chance of emptying the hand ([the model](#a-model-of-the-choices)); - the doubled pool lets it complete an island or reach domination this turn (foresight).

requirement: Each computer seat adds `W_LEADER` (by level) to the value of battles and raids against a leader. The test is one formula for every seat: a human leader and a computer leader are treated alike, and a computer seat that is itself the leader plays for the win. The view does not say which seats are human, so the check cannot single one out. The adjusted count keeps a handicap the players chose from counting as a runaway; the near-win test reads real countries, because a seat at 28 is seven captures from winning however it got there.
